job.description:
Warehouse Manager – Auckland

Lead a busy distribution centre. Keep stock moving. Deliver exceptional service.

Our client is looking for a hands-on, organised Warehouse Manager to lead the day-to-day operation of our Auckland distribution centre. This is a practical role for someone who enjoys taking ownership, working alongside their team and making sure every order, delivery and stock movement is completed accurately and on time.

The opportunity

You will keep the warehouse safe, tidy and ready for the next arrival while maintaining strong communication with customers, freight providers and the wider business.

What you’ll be responsible for

  • Running daily warehouse operations so orders are picked, processed, invoiced and despatched on time
  • Managing inwards goods, container devanning, stock receipting and allocated storage space
  • Maintaining accurate stock control, including weekly stocktakes and FIFO practices
  • Coordinating effectively freight partners
  • Keeping container documentation, MPI requirements, records and reporting up to date
  • Leading from the floor, supporting the team and maintaining a clean, efficient warehouse
  • Operating forklift, clamp and reach equipment to a safe and capable standard

What you’ll bring

  • Experience coordinating or leading warehouse and distribution operations
  • Strong organisation, follow-through and attention to detail
  • A practical understanding of stock control, despatch and freight processes
  • Confidence using warehouse systems, spreadsheets and everyday computer tools
  • Clear, professional communication and a customer-service mindset
  • A collaborative approach, with a focus on continuous improvement and getting the job done
  • The ability to operate forklift, clamp and reach equipment; relevant current licences or endorsements are highly regarded

Why this role?

This is an opportunity to take real ownership of a busy Auckland operation where accuracy, teamwork and reliable service matter every day. You will have the scope to improve how the warehouse runs, build strong working relationships and see the direct impact of your leadership.

Ready to lead from the front? Apply with your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your warehouse leadership experience and what you would bring to the team.

job.title: Mig Welding
job.description:
Step into a hands-on welding role where your precision and technical expertise directly support high-quality fabrication work for a busy Wellington workshop.

This fixed-term opportunity is ideal for a skilled MIG welder who thrives in a safety-focused environment and takes pride in producing clean, reliable welds to specification.

About the Role:
You will carry out MIG welding and associated fabrication tasks to deliver components and structures that meet strict quality and safety standards.
Working from blueprints and technical drawings, you will ensure accurate interpretation and execution, contributing to efficient project delivery and minimal rework.

Key Responsibilities:
* Perform MIG welding on a variety of metals in accordance with job specifications and workshop procedures.
* Interpret blueprints and technical drawings to determine welding sequences, dimensions, and fabrication requirements.
* Carry out metal preparation, cutting, and fitting to ensure correct alignment and joint configuration before welding.
* Use welding and workshop tools, including grinders, clamps, and measuring equipment, to support fabrication and finishing.
* Inspect welds for defects, identify root causes, and carry out repairs to restore structural integrity and appearance.
* Conduct weld quality checks and basic non-destructive testing as required to verify compliance with standards.
* Maintain a clean, organised work area and handle equipment in line with workshop safety protocols.
* Collaborate with supervisors and team members to meet production targets and adjust work plans as jobs progress.

Key Requirements:
* Proven experience in MIG welding in a fabrication or workshop environment.
* Strong ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, and welding symbols.
* Practical experience in metal fabrication, cutting, and fitting for welded assemblies.
* Solid understanding of welding safety standards and safe workshop practices.
* Competence in identifying common weld defects and carrying out effective repair techniques.
* Familiarity with basic weld inspection methods and quality control procedures.
* Reliable, detail-focused approach with the ability to work to set timeframes on a fixed-term basis.

Desirable Skills:
* Exposure to working with different materials and metallurgical properties in welding applications.
* Experience with basic non-destructive testing methods for weld quality assessment.
* Ability to suggest improvements in fabrication processes to reduce defects and rework.
* Previous experience in a similar role within a production or engineering workshop in New Zealand.

Qualifications:
* Trade qualification or certificate in welding, fabrication, or a related discipline is preferred.
* Recognised MIG welding tickets or certifications are advantageous.
* Relevant health and safety training (e.g. workshop safety, hazard management) is beneficial.

If you are a skilled MIG welder looking to contribute to quality fabrication work on a fixed-term basis in Wellington, we’d like to hear from you.
